html:
A diamond mining and trading company founded in 1888 by Cecil Rhodes at Kimberley in southern Africa. It took its name from the farm of the De Beer brothers, where diamonds were found in the Kimberley diamond rush.

With money from the Rothschilds, Rhodes bought out his rival Barney Barnato and merged the mines into one company. De Beers soon controlled nearly all diamond production in southern Africa. Its profits helped fund Rhodes's British South Africa Company and his push north.

In 1929 Ernest Oppenheimer of Anglo American took control. Through a London selling organisation, De Beers held back supply to keep prices high and for most of the 1900s controlled most of the world's rough diamond trade. Its 1947 slogan "A Diamond Is Forever" helped make the diamond engagement ring a custom. It later went into partnership with Botswana, home of the Orapa mine, and its grip on the market loosened after 2000.
